base_member_text: w computation (L88-93): both divx and divy come from diff() with no dimension argument, differencing along the first (row/y) dimension for both terms -- so w=-diff_y(h*u)/dx-diff_y(h*v)/dy rather than a proper 2D divergence; also diff shortens the first dimension by 1 while sampling still uses full-grid indices jg (L100-102), a 1-row misalignment.
audit_member_text: Both divx and divy use diff with no dimension argument at L88-L91, so MATLAB differences both fluxes along the first nonsingleton dimension; the x-flux is not differenced along the second grid dimension even though L92-L93 divide it by dx.

jg can be assigned iy+1=ny at L53, but w1 and w2 have one fewer row because diff defaults to the first dimension at L88-L91; sampling w1/w2 at L100 or L102 can therefore exceed their row range for a gauge mapped to row ny.

base_member_text: nearest-index search (L47-69) leaves ig/jg undefined for gauges outside the axis ranges; no guard; igjg.mat cache can silently go stale when the grid changes (only the interactive flag L45 controls refresh).
audit_member_text: ig and jg are only assigned when each gauge falls into one of the half-open cell intervals scanned at L48-L67; if a coordinate lies outside or exactly at an uncovered boundary, the later samples at L96-L102 use an unassigned element.

base_member_text: The kg==18 special case uses the deeper level w1 (hh1=0.03+dep) while all others use w2 (hh2=0.01+dep) (L99-103) -- ADV elevation rationale not in the file.
hh1/hh2 add constants to the full depth array; interpretation (sensor heights above bed 3 cm/1 cm?) is not stated.
FSE output selects gauges 1,3,6,7,9,12,13,15,17 (L109-117) to form 9 columns matching the WG1-9 comparison in plot_WG.m; mapping justified only implicitly.

audit_member_text: The same unqualified diff operations yield arrays reduced only in rows, so divx and divy happen to have matching shapes but do not represent orthogonal derivatives; this masks the axis mismatch rather than producing a dimension error.
